task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of March 27, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: Pharos BioClinical halted enrollment and dosing in its Phase 2 trial of Vectirex (VCX-421) on March 27, 2025, after an independent safety monitoring board identified a liver enzyme elevation signal.
Eight of 312 enrolled patients developed alanine aminotransferase levels more than five times the upper limit of normal, a threshold the trial protocol designated as a stopping criterion.
Vectirex is a peptide-synthase inhibitor designed to target gram-negative bacteria that have developed resistance to existing antibiotics.
The drug's mechanism differs from all currently approved antibiotic classes, which Pharos says offers potential against bacteria resistant to carbapenems and colistin.

The data safety monitoring board chair, Dr. Noel Adeyemi, said the board acted on pre-specified stopping rules rather than a clinical judgment call, noting that the liver findings warranted investigation before the trial could continue.
Pharos chief medical officer Dr. Amanda Yee said: "We are disappointed by this setback, but the DSMB's recommendation is exactly why independent oversight exists. Patient safety must come first."
All eight patients with elevated enzymes were taken off the drug; six of the eight showed enzyme levels returning toward normal within two weeks, according to the company.

Pharos said it does not know whether the elevations are dose-related, class-related, or affect a specific patient subgroup, and will analyze blood samples before deciding whether to modify the trial or abandon the compound.
Vectirex had shown activity against 14 drug-resistant bacterial strains in Phase 1 testing, which enrolled 80 healthy volunteers and identified no liver signal.
The halt does not affect patients who completed the trial regimen; it applies to current dosing and new enrollments.

Infectious disease specialist Dr. Rina Okafor, not affiliated with the trial, said gram-negative antibiotic resistance kills an estimated 700,000 people globally each year and new drug classes are critically needed, but that safety signals in this class are not unexpected given the mechanism's novelty.
Pharos has invested approximately $340 million in Vectirex development over six years.
The company said it does not have a timeline for when it will decide whether to resume the trial or close the VCX-421 program.
Pharos's stock fell 22% in after-hours trading on the day of the announcement.
Regulatory agencies in three countries had granted Vectirex fast-track or priority designation based on its target indication.
The National Institutes of Health had contributed $28 million in preclinical funding to the Vectirex program before Pharos acquired the compound from a university spin-off.
No other companies are known to be developing drugs in the peptide-synthase inhibitor class as of the trial halt date.
Pharos said it will file a full safety report with regulators within 30 days.
The eight patients who showed enzyme elevations were enrolled across five different trial sites in three countries.
Dr. Adeyemi said in a statement that the monitoring board's decision was unanimous.

forbidden_additions: a claim that Vectirex caused permanent liver damage
a statement that the trial will be permanently closed
casualty figures for the enrolled patients
